stances_toward.note: AUKUS partner and Five Eyes: the Geelong Treaty of 26 Jul 2025 is a 50-year bilateral treaty for the SSN-AUKUS submarine (worth up to GBP 20bn of British exports over 25 years); the Pentagon's AUKUS review (Dec 2025) found ways to put the deal on the 'strongest possible footing' and both Canberra and London were still working through it. The UK hoped the bilateral treaty would hold the US to the trilateral. Bond - kin: Anglosphere, Commonwealth, shared service history.

stances_toward.note: Partner at its closest: the Australia-Indonesia Treaty on Common Security (signed in Jakarta, 6 Feb 2026) obliges regular leader and ministerial consultation on security and builds on the 2006 Lombok Treaty and a 2024 defence cooperation agreement; analysts (ASPI's Graham) call it modest, with no common-danger clause, unlike Australia's treaty with Papua New Guinea. Not an alliance. Indonesia still wants Papua respected as its own affair and the East Timor memory sits under the relation, but no 2025-26 source names a grievance; bond - none.

The Indian trade deficit with Australia fell to USD 6.5bn in FY2026 under the ECTA. Quad partner. Bond - none.

stances_toward.note: The largest defence-industrial deal in the relationship: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries' Mogami design chosen on 5 Aug 2025 over Germany's MEKO A-200, contract for the first three of eleven general-purpose frigates signed in April 2026 (AUD 10bn / about USD 6.5bn programme). Both are US allies and Quad members and Takaichi went on to Australia after Hanoi. Held at partner because there is no mutual-defence obligation between them; reading as 'quasi-allied' is common but we found no source using the label.
